title: Pow(x, n)
summary: Compute x raised to the integer exponent n.

contractDetails.constraints: −100 < x < 100, n is signed 32-bit, x is nonzero or n is positive, and the mathematical result lies in [−10000,10000].
contractDetails.output-checking: Require a finite numeric result within relative tolerance 10⁻⁶ or absolute tolerance 10⁻¹².

statement: Compute x raised to the integer exponent n. A negative exponent means taking a reciprocal.

examples.explanation: An odd exponent keeps the negative sign.

constraints: −100 < x < 100, n is signed 32-bit, x is nonzero or n is positive, and the mathematical result lies in [−10000,10000].
hints: Conceptual: Repeated squaring doubles the exponent in one step.
Directional: Handle negative exponents by using the reciprocal base.
Implementation: Accumulate the factor when the exponent is odd. Halve the exponent each round and widen it before negating the signed minimum.
complexityAnalysis: O(log(|n| + 1)) time and O(1) extra space.
